replies:
You don't have a resume on file here yet. Paste your resume (or upload it), and I will read it and save its entries. If you want a quick checklist now, here are the most common gaps I look for on resumes for Junior Software Engineer roles — use it to self-check while you paste:
1) Name, email and LinkedIn/GitHub links at the top — contact must be exact and professional.
2) One-line summary (optional) that states role sought (e.g., "Junior Software Engineer") and top stack.
3) Clear, reverse-chron experience entries with: employer, title, dates (month/year), 3–6 bullet points each that focus on outcomes and use metrics (load, % improvement, users, tests). Show code contributions, not only tasks.
4) Projects section with links to GitHub or deployed apps, each with tech stack, problem solved, your role and one measurable result or demo link. At least 2–4 projects if professional experience is limited.
5) Skills list split into: Languages, Frameworks/Tools, Databases, DevOps/CI, Testing; be honest and specific (e.g., "Python (Django), JavaScript (React, Node), PostgreSQL, Docker, Jest").
6) One or two concrete wins from internships/class projects (bug fixed, feature shipped, performance improved) quantified where possible.
7) Tests and engineering practices: mention TDD, unit/integration tests, CI pipelines, code review, pair programming if you used them.
8) Education with degree, school, graduation date; include relevant coursework only if short on experience (algorithms, OS, data structures).
9) Keywords from job postings you target (React, REST, SQL, cloud provider) — tailored for each application.
10) Concise formatting: one page (junior), readable font, bullet-first verbs (Implemented, Built, Reduced), no paragraph blocks.
11) Links to profiles that show activity: GitHub with recent commits, portfolio/demo, and a short README per project explaining how to run it.
12) Proof of collaboration: mention team size, SCRUM, or cross-functional work; evidence you worked in a codebase (PRs, reviews).
13) Remove irrelevant details (high school, unrelated jobs) unless they show transferable skills with outcomes.
14) Optional but strong: contributions to open-source, hackathon prizes, or coding challenge ranks (LeetCode/Codeforces) if you can back them up.

Paste your resume now and I will:
- read it and save every entry as draft facts,
- tell you in two lines what I read (latest role, top skills, education),
- give 2–3 concrete changes to make it stronger for Junior Software Engineer roles,
- offer to search for matching jobs.

You're in final rounds at Lincoln International for an analyst role. Tell me one thing first: do you already have the interview date/time and format (video, in-person, panel, case, technical)? If yes, type it once; if not, say "not yet" and I'll assume a 60–90 minute virtual final with 2–4 interviewers including one senior banker and an HR/fit interviewer.

Prep plan now (I’ll run through this with you, starting with question practice and a short company brief):
1) Quick brief (2–3 lines) I’ll use in answers
- What Lincoln International does, the analyst role’s focus, and likely interviewer priorities (technical modeling, deal experience/fit, cultural fit, stamina for long hours). I’ll assume M&A advisory mid‑market unless you say otherwise.
2) Top 6 final-round questions you must nail — I’ll quiz you on them, then score and improve each answer:
- Walk me through your resume / why Lincoln?
- Tell me about a deal or project you worked on — your role, challenge, outcome. (STAR + metrics)
- Valuation / technical: how do you value a company? Walk me through DCF steps and sensitivities.
- Accounting deep-dive: if revenue rises 10% but NWC increases 20%, how does FCF change? (or similar)
- Case: here’s a company with [brief financials], what would you do? (framework + quick numbers)
- Strengths/weaknesses and why we should hire you / handling long hours & team conflicts
3) Tailored scorecard I’ll use when you answer: structure, evidence (numbers/specifics), and interviewer signals (concise vs. curious). After each answer I give one concrete fix.

4) Two short scripts you can adapt (30–45 seconds) — a) 1-minute "why Lincoln" and b) 45-second "deal walkthrough" that hit action + impact + numbers.
5) Quick technical checklist (things to have crisp and practice aloud):
- DCF steps and assumptions (WACC, terminal growth vs. exit multiple)
- Three valuation methods and when each dominates
- Accruals -> cash bridges: EBITDA -> Net Income -> FCF
- LBO basics (if relevant): equity check, sources & uses, IRR drivers
- Quick math: margins, growth rates, comps multiples intuition
- How to build sensitivity tables and what they show
6) Day-of tactics (brief):
- Bring one printed 1-page deal bullet sheet and your resume (if in-person).
- Open with 30–60s crisp intro; ask 1–2 smart questions per interviewer (one about deal flow/sector focus, one about mentorship/career path).
- If given a case, speak your framework first, call out assumptions, do a 2–3 minute topline recommendation before digging into numbers.
Next step: pick one of these and we’ll practice now.
- A: Ask me to quiz you on "walk me through your resume" and I’ll ask it, then score.
- B: Send your 1-minute "why Lincoln" answer and I’ll score and rewrite it.
- C: Tell me the interview format (time and panel) and I’ll give the one-page brief and 10-point prep plan for that exact format.

One question: which option now — A, B or C?

Here’s exactly what I will fill, field by field, for the first posting you pick. I state what I will put (using only your confirmed facts) and what I will leave as [brackets] for you to provide on the application card before anything is submitted.

  - What I will put: the exact link the search returned.

- Field: Cover letter / message body (<=120 words for an email)
  - What I will put: a short tailored message drafted from the posting and your confirmed facts with this structure:
    1) One opening sentence stating the role and one key reason you fit (skill/experience).
    2) One sentence with 1–2 achievements that match a top requirement (numbers where possible).
    3) One closing sentence about next steps and your availability.
  - Any item I don’t know (specific availability, exact notice period) I will leave as [Your availability, e.g. "immediately" or "2 weeks' notice"].
5) Screening / application questions
- Field: Yes/no, multiple choice, and short-text answers

6) Work authorization / visa status
- Field: Work authorization
  - What I will put: [your exact words about authorization] — left blank until you provide them. I will not guess or assume sponsorship needs.
7) Desired salary / pay expectations
- Field: Desired salary
  - What I will put: [your stated pay floor] or blank if you haven’t given one. I will include pay only when you confirm the number.

  - What I will put: the contact name and email only if you give it or it’s listed on the posting; otherwise left empty.

  - What I will put: exact posting URL.
- Field: Timestamp and persona used
  - What I will put: timestamp set when you approve the card, and the resume persona name you pick (or 'base').

- I will not invent dates, authorization, salary, contacts, or resume contact details.

- I will not attach files I don’t explicitly have.
